{{short description|Polish mathematician}}
'''Zdzisław Jan Ewangelii Antoni Krygowski''' ([[Lwów]], 1872 — 1955, [[Poznań]]) was a Polish mathematician, [[Rector (academia)|rector]] of the [[Lviv Polytechnic|Lwów Polytechnic]] (1917–18), and professor at [[Poznań University]] (1919–38, 1946–55).

==Enigma==
Krygowski has become famous in the history of [[cryptology]] for having assisted the [[General Staff of the Polish Army|Polish General Staff]] in setting up its cryptology course for [[Poznań University]] mathematics students that began on 15 January 1929. This led eventually to the General Staff's [[Biuro Szyfrów|Cipher Bureau]]'s recruitment of [[Marian Rejewski]], [[Henryk Zygalski]] and [[Jerzy Różycki]], who would jointly break and [[decryption|decrypt]] the [[World War II]]-era [[Germany|German]] [[Enigma machine|Enigma-machine ciphers]], beginning at the end of December 1932.<ref>See "[[Marian Rejewski#Citations|Marian Rejewski]]," footnote citation no. 1.</ref>

==Family==
Zdzisław Krygowski had three brothers - Tadeusz, Kazimierz and Stanisław.
He married Rose New from England. They had one daughter Eileen Krygowska-Korczyńska, who after World War II worked for [[Jan Nowak-Jeziorański]] at [[Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty|RFE]].
